---
title: "Install and launch"
---

## What you'll need

- Python 3.11 or newer and [*uv*](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) to install and manage the application (you can also use `pip` directly, but *uv* makes things easy!).
- A folder containing supported *TOFWERK* *TOFexplorer* HDF5 (`.h5`) acquisitions.
- A writable folder with enough space for saved acquisition copies.

## Installation

After installing `uv` using the instructions for your operating system at the link above, you can open a new terminal window and check that it is available:

```sh
uv --version
```

The following command installs ToFScope from PyPI:

```sh
uv tool install tofscope
```

If your shell cannot find `tofscope`, you can run `uv tool update-shell` and open a new terminal window.

## Folder selection and launch

By default, ToFScope will only have access to whatever files are in the folder that you launch it from
(or any subfolders). You can use the `--data-root` argument to allow read-only access to another folder
(such as a network mount containing your instruments' data) and the `--output-root` argument to allow
for saving analysis results to a separate folder.

The example paths in this command should be replaced with your acquisition and saved-copy folders;
paths containing spaces need quotation marks:

```sh
tofscope --data-root "/path/to/acquisitions" --output-root "/path/to/saved-analyses"
```

The local service will start in your terminal and the app should open automatically in your browser.
The terminal process needs to remain open while you work. After saving your analysis, you can stop the
service by returning to the terminal and pressing **Ctrl-C**.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Saving before stopping the service

Heads up! Open analyses and in-progress jobs are held in memory until you explicitly save them.
Use the **Save as** feature to save your analysis before stopping the ToFScope process, or you will
lose your data!
:::

Original acquisitions opened by ToFScope are never edited directly; the applicaiton will only save copies
to protect the original integrity of the collected data.

## Updates and removal

Using *uv*, the app can be updated with the following command:

```sh
uv tool upgrade tofscope
```

The command `uv tool uninstall tofscope` uninstalls the app. This does not delete your acquisition or saved-analysis folders.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| **`uv: command not found`** | A new terminal window and the PATH instructions printed by the uv installer may resolve the problem. |
| **`tofscope: command not found`** | You can run `uv tool update-shell`, open a new terminal window, and try again. `uv tool list` shows installed tools. |
| **No files in the picker** | `--data-root` must point to the folder containing the `.h5` files, and the service needs permission to read it. If `--data-root` is not given, ToFScope can only see files within the folder from which it was run. |
| **Browser did not open** | The terminal may contain an error message. If the service is running, `tofscope open` in another terminal window opens the existing local service. |
| **Cannot save** | The output folder must exist, be writable, and have enough free space for a full copy. Calculations must be finished or canceled and drafts finished or discarded before saving. ToFScope also will not overwrite a file, currently, so check if there is a duplicate file name in the selected folder. |
| **Port already in use** | The previous ToFScope process may need to be stopped before trying again. |

For help with startup problems, `tofscope doctor` loads the configuration and verifies the packaged frontend assets. It reports an error if either check fails; it does not diagnose every startup problem:

```sh
tofscope doctor --data-root "/path/to/acquisitions" --output-root "/path/to/saved-analyses"
```
